title: Pirate Chain (ARRR) — forged coin-import mint; two on-chain mints ~79.8M ARRR; exits closed

conditional_eu.trigger: any CEX or verified instant-swap/bridge deposit rail reopens on the legacy chain that contains the forged imports
conditional_eu.race_risk: high — hard fork/reindex, chain split, exchange freeze, thin liquidity

closed_reasons: MEXC ARRR deposits and withdrawals suspended 2026-10-15 at the project's request
NonKYC ARRR depositActive=false / withdrawalActive=false ('By request of the Pirate Chain devs')
ChangeNOW supports only BSC-wrapped ARRR; native ARRR unsupported and ARRR(BSC)->BTC returns PAIR_NOT_AVAILABLE
Godex does not list ARRR; other instant swappers are key-gated/unverified
vARRR/Verus bridge hacked 2026-05-18 ($11.58M); ARRR<->vARRR liquidity unverified
Base 'ARRR' token 0x6145...7bd2 is a 1B-supply impostor, not the real 200M-cap coin
No public ARRR OTC desk; private bilateral only
Chain is split/stalled: explorer follows the legacy chain; 10/57 patched peers are not on its tip
key_facts: Vulnerable code: v6.0.0-v6.0.9; ConnectBlock used if (tx.IsMint()) instead of if (tx.IsCoinBase()), so coin imports skipped ContextualCheckInputs -> VerifyCoinImport (no proof-of-burn).
Mempool rejects forged imports: AcceptToMemoryPool calls ContextualCheckInputs unconditionally; the tx must be placed directly in a block by a miner.

Fix commit da4e6252a3 (2026-10-14 23:50Z) changes the branch to IsCoinBase() and adds a regression test that expects invalid-coin-import; v6.0.10 released 2026-10-18 23:48Z (mandatory reindex); v6.0.11 (2026-10-19 21:19Z) is networking-only.
The official 39.8M figure is only the first mint; the second +40.0M on 2026-10-16 is not in the official statement or public coverage found.
Total forged: 79,822,592 ARRR, ~$19.60M at $0.2455 (first mint alone ~$9.77M).
Patch adoption in a 57-peer sample: 10 on 6.0.10 (17.5%), 28 on vulnerable 6.0.0-6.0.9 (49.1%), 19 pre-6.0.0 stuck (33.3%); only 6/57 on the explorer tip.
Network: 1.921 MSol/s, 60.3s blocks, 0.25 ARRR reward (~$0.061), 358 ARRR/day (~$88/day).
Rented-hash cost: ~$0.069 per expected block; 51% of the network ~$50/day at NiceHash Equihash prices (~$51,429/GSol/day).
Exit liquidity: Gate 24h $14,743 / book $6.6k bid-$9.2k ask; MEXC $64,664 / $9.4k-$15.1k; NonKYC ~$430k/day; tracked total ~$509k/day, ~38x smaller than the $19.6M notional.
NonKYC froze the first attempted deposit; no confirmed attacker realization.
caveats: The explorer's node data is 9 hours stale at read time (updated 2026-10-19 14:21Z) and the network is split; the total supply is the explorer node's pool sum, not an independent UTXO audit.

The second +40M is inferred from the explorer's daily pool jump; a full-node block scan/UTXO audit should confirm the exact txids. If it is an indexer correction rather than a second mint, the 278.8M supply remains but the 'two mints' attribution would change.
The 57-peer version sample is from one explorer node, not a network census; the 17.5% patched share has selection bias.
NiceHash rental prices are an external snapshot (2026-10-17/18) and liquidity varies; the <$1/block conclusion is robust to a 10x price range.
Realizable value ($1.0-2.9M) is a low-confidence judgment, not an on-chain quantity.
No transactions were signed or sent; no exchange accounts, KYC or OTC contact.

mining_cost.note: Cost per expected block is independent of share; 51% for a day is ~$50.

one_liner: External unprivileged attacker can extract $0 live: the Pirate Chain coin-import mint is still live on <=v6.0.9 miners and total supply is 278.8M ARRR (139.4% of the 200M cap; 79.8M forged across two mints, ~$19.6M notional), but every CEX deposit rail is closed and no verified instant-swap/bridge exists; if one reopens on the legacy chain, a realistic $1.0-2.9M is capturable before the hard fork/reindex, with high race and freeze risk.
